stumbles.quote: Jev will not review declaude_lint's hits on public posts.
stumbles.why: declaude_lint is never explained (what it is, what a 'hit' or 'tic' means). Jev's role is also unclear until later.

stumbles.quote: Oskar asked on 2026-11-07, "Should we implement Jev in our public posting review process?"
stumbles.why: Oskar is not introduced. The question refers to a review process that the text doesn't describe.

stumbles.quote: With the tic's definition from register.md in its prompt
stumbles.why: register.md is never explained, and neither is the definition of 'tic' it holds. 'The tic' reads as if a particular tic had already been named.

stumbles.quote: Jev ranked the hits at AUROC 0.808.
stumbles.why: The text doesn't say what the ranking is for. It also doesn't say whether the 0.808 figure is above or below any benchmark until the baseline follows.

stumbles.quote: so at a 5% error budget it could settle only 24.5% of hits
stumbles.why: 'Settle' and 'error budget' are not defined. The reader can't tell how a probability becomes a settled hit, or what the 5% applies to.

stumbles.quote: The bar set in advance was 50%.
stumbles.why: The text never says who set the bar or why it was 50%. It also doesn't say whether the bar refers to the share of hits settled.

stumbles.quote: The lint's own precision varies by rule: 5 of 44 triad hits were real tics, 5 of 43 participle hits, and 16 of 18 negation-first hits.
stumbles.why: The rules are not defined (triad, participle, negation-first). The counts total 105 hits, so it's unclear how they relate to the 261 agreed hits or the 35.2% rate. It's also unclear whether they are the baseline's categories.

stumbles.quote: Jev is not added to the review.
stumbles.why: This contradicts the opening, 'Jev will not review', only in tense and framing. The reader can't tell whether Jev was ever part of the review or was only proposed.

point: Jev, a small calibrated decision model, was tested as a reviewer of lint hits on public posts. It settled only 24.5% of hits at a 5% error budget, well short of the 50% bar, and barely beat a category-only baseline, so it was not adopted.
